What public sources could not show

  1. Current Visa VSS user guides, the live VSS report catalogue and VOIP invoice screens Visa marks VSS guides confidential and keeps VOIP inside Visa Online. A 2018 guide posted openly by a third party shows the reports, but the current screens are not public. A processor client manual that quotes current VSS layouts, or a Visa client partner under NDA.
  2. Visa's Acquirer Billing Guide and Mastercard's billing event catalogue Both are client-only and known here through the UK regulator's decision. Watch for the schemes' ITC Compliance Policy letters due about end of October 2026 and the Standard A fee guides due July 2027.
  3. The current Mastercard MCBS manual, invoice layout and Billing Analytic Tool screens They sit behind Mastercard Connect. A 2020 Settlement Manual is openly readable, but the billing tools show no fields in public. Sponsor bank onboarding guides, Mastercard Academy seminar material or PSR compliance publications from mid 2027.
  4. Mastercard Performance Insights, portfolio analytics and acquirer dashboards mastercard.com and mastercardservices.com returned 403 to scripted fetches, which were not bypassed. A normal browser session by hand, later Wayback captures, or webinar captions.
  5. PULSE settlement agent, cutoff, settlement reports, Operating Rules and Issuer Fee Schedule They live on the PULSE client site. Only FIS processor reports and marketing pages are public. Credit union or bank board papers and core processor guides that cite PULSE settlement.
  6. Current Discover Network acquirer settlement reports and service centre screens Behind login. Public material is a 2003 report sample and a 2007 archived help page. Settlement instruction PDFs returned 403 and were not bypassed. An acquirer login, or processor manuals republished by banks or state agencies.
  7. The OptBlue participant settlement files and the US wholesale bill as a participant receives it The 2024 regulations and two processors' pricing guides are openly posted, but no actual bill or file layout is. An OptBlue Participant contract or a procurement bid that attaches it.
  8. Real ATM operator statements and portal screens from CDS, Switch Commerce and Cardtronics Portals sit behind login and no public sample statement surfaced. Ask an ISO partner or NAC member for a redacted statement and portal walk-through.
  9. Merchant statement layouts at Fiserv and Clover, Worldpay, Chase, Global Payments and Elavon Public help pages returned 404, 403 or login walls. State procurement attachments or sample statements in public RFP responses.
  10. How US credit unions and community banks book daily network settlement to the general ledger Only two job postings and the FIS report guide were found. CUSO and corporate credit union procedure guides, and card settlement analyst postings.
  11. Diners Club franchise-to-franchise settlement and NYCE, CO-OP and Accel reporting No public manuals found, and the shared search budget ran out before CO-OP and Accel. Licensee filings for Diners, and a fresh search of credit union and processor documents.
  12. Whether Mastercard renamed GCMS and still runs Sunday cycles A 2026 vendor blog and Paymentology conflict with the 2021 manual. A 2025 or 2026 clearing manual republished by a processor.

Run: disputes and fraud

Every network runs the same skeleton: a fraud report or claim, a chargeback, a response, pre-arbitration, then a ruling. Each wraps it in its own tool, vocabulary and clock (Visa Core Rules · Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition · Business and Operational Policies · Dispute Ticket Retrieval Request · Best Practices for Disputes). Mastercard is the most visible. Its public Mastercom spec names 13 work queues, case statuses from New to Ruled, and hard edits that reject late cycles (Mastercom Testing · Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI · Mastercom Code and Formats · Mastercom). Visa keeps VROL screens and API states restricted. What partners see is inferred from processor portals that mirror VROL statuses, questionnaires and buttons (Visa Resolve Online · iQ Reporting and Analytics · iQ Reporting and Analytics · Managing Visa Disputes). American Express publishes the clearest merchant dispute screen. Its summary table sorts cases into Response Needed, Review in Progress and Closed, and each case shows days left to respond (How to use · Managing a Dispute Case). The contest has moved before the chargeback. Visa switched Rapid Dispute Resolution on for issuers by default, and Mastercard pulls Ethoca data into the claim itself (Rapid Dispute Resolution · Compelling Evidence 3.0 · Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI · Mastercard Rules). Monitoring now counts fraud and disputes together at portfolio level, and merchants and payfacs cannot see the items behind their own ratio (Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program · New VAMP for 2025 · Dispute and fraud card · Mastercard GMAP Explained). Small issuers, fintechs and most merchants never touch a network dispute tool. Processors translate network stages into their own states, windows and codes (Card Dispute Consultant · Chargebacks · Disputes · Worldpay Disputes API · What Is Visa Resolve). The Discover family is the least visible. Its Disputes Portal sits behind a login, its public merchant help page lists Internet Explorer 6, and PULSE dispute rules need a login (Discover Global Network · Dispute System Interface · Best Practices for Disputes). The strongest openings for Discover are one shared case vocabulary, a published monitoring line, free pre-dispute resolution, and fraud reporting folded into the dispute (Discover Chargeback Guide · Discover Chargebacks · Fraud Management Tools · Mastercom Use Cases).

Design moves at this stage

6b.1Show whose move it is and the days left, on every caseStrong evidence
The move
Make the case status a next action with an owner and a day count, drawn from the condition's own time limit. Publish the same states through the API.
Why it wins
Amex and a PULSE processor wrapper already show next action and days left. Each fintech processor invents its own states, so one network vocabulary would travel across all of them. Discover's portal already shows a Stage Expiration date, but its Dispute Status values name system results and never the next actor. (Managing a Dispute Case · Disputes (PULSE) · Chargebacks · Disputes · Managing Visa Disputes · Visa Core Rules · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Issuers: large banks, Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors, Fintechs and programme managers, Merchants where they touch the network directly
6b.2Fold fraud reporting into the disputeStrong evidence
The move
Let one issuer action file the fraud report and open the dispute, instead of a separate Confirmed Fraud portal.
Why it wins
Visa and Mastercard both require the fraud report first, and Visa penalises reporting failures by suspending dispute rights. Mastercard already files the report from inside the claim. Mastercom lists a fraud report among claim actions, while Discover's portal offers only retrieval, chargeback and compliance tabs. (Visa Core Rules · Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition · Mastercom Use Cases · Confirmed Fraud Portal Access · Mastercom User Guide · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Issuers: large banks, Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Fintechs and programme managers
6b.3Offer free pre-dispute resolution and count it as preventedStrong evidence
The move
Route every new claim through a merchant resolution step first, at no per-alert fee, and show resolved claims as prevented on partner reports.
Why it wins
Visa auto-enrolled issuers in RDR and excludes pre-dispute resolutions from monitoring. Merchants pay per alert elsewhere, and Mastercard's acquirer route is reported to be ending. (Rapid Dispute Resolution · Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program · Mastercard Rules · Chargeback Alerts Compared · Chargeback alert pricing hides · Mastercard Acquirer Collaboration Ends · Discover Chargebacks · Fraud Management Tools)
For
Issuers: large banks, Acquirers and processors, Merchants where they touch the network directly
6b.4Publish the monitoring line and show the items behind the ratioStrong evidence
The move
Publish Discover's dispute and fraud thresholds. Give acquirers a live ratio per merchant and sub-merchant with every counted item listed.
Why it wins
Merchants cannot see the items behind VAMP and data arrives a month late. Discover has no public line at all, so publishing one closes a gap competitors leave open. (New VAMP for 2025 · Dispute and fraud card · Discover Chargeback Guide · Exploring the Chargeback Threshold · Mastercard GMAP Explained · Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program)
For
Acquirers and processors, Payment facilitators and ISOs, Merchants where they touch the network directly
6b.5Make the dispute rules public and datedStrong evidence
The move
Publish the Discover and PULSE dispute rules and time limits openly, with effective dates on each change.
Why it wins
Mastercard publishes its Chargeback Guide and Visa its core rules. Discover and PULSE keep theirs gated, so practitioners fill the gap with secondhand figures. Discover's merchant dispute manual, marked proprietary and confidential, sat openly on its service centre site, so keeping procedures private protects little. Discover's portal shows some reason codes differently from its rules manual, so published rules need one code list shared with the screens. (Mastercard Rules for Merchants · Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition · Visa Core Rules · Best Practices for Disputes · Discover Card Dispute · Discover Chargebacks · Discover Network Dispute System · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Acquirers and processors, Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Fintechs and programme managers, Developers
6b.6Put the partner's own legal clock beside the network clockModerate evidence
The move
Show Reg E provisional credit and decision deadlines next to chargeback deadlines on each issuer case, starting from the cardholder contact date.
Why it wins
Issuers run two sets of deadlines. The only public tool that warns on the Reg E deadline is a processor portal, so a network that does it serves small issuers directly. (§ 1005.11 Procedures · 12 CFR 1005.11, Procedures · About Regulation E · Card Dispute Consultant)
For
Issuers: large banks, Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Fintechs and programme managers
6b.7Let the cardholder start the claim and let the network set the clockModerate evidence
The move
Offer issuers a network-hosted claim start they can embed in their app, feeding the case with a network-set timer for each step.
Why it wins
Pix mandates in-app self-service with central-bank timers. Card claims still start by phone or branch, and some fintechs see them a day late. (Guia de implementação · FINBOA is revolutionizing payment · Disputes · How to lessen)
For
Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Fintechs and programme managers
6b.8Let evidence be checked before it is finalModerate evidence
The move
Validate evidence against the reason code before submission, show limits up front, and list items still missing inside the window.
Why it wins
CE3.0 and Stripe Issuing allow one attempt. Upload caps range from three images to 18 MB. Mastercom's Pending Documentation Report shows the value of flagging gaps early. Discover raised uploads from 3 MB images to 15 MB files, yet conditional mandatory fields still error only on submit. (Compelling Evidence 3.0 Acquirer · Issuing disputes · Dispute System Interface · Image and Document Requirements · Adding Documents · Mastercom Extended Announcements · Discover Network Dispute System · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Acquirers and processors, Merchants where they touch the network directly, Fintechs and programme managers
6b.9Deliver compromise alerts as actionsModerate evidence
The move
Send compromised-card alerts as a list with block, monitor and reissue actions per card, by screen and API, with the recovery deadline shown.
Why it wins
Credit unions reformat alert lists by hand several times a week. Vendors now sell tools against that work, and loss recovery depends on reporting within 120 days. (CU*BASE and Compromised Cards · CAMS Alert Manager · Velera Launches Risk Alert · Account Data Compromise Best · Account Incident Manager (AIM))
For
Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Issuers: large banks
6b.10One sign-in and self-serve enrolment for dispute and fraud toolsModerate evidence
The move
Put the Disputes Portal and the Fraud and Risk Center under one identity, with administrators granting access online.
Why it wins
Discover's fraud tools need signed forms and email-only MFA, while the Disputes Portal already uses the shared identity provider. The DN Disputes Portal already runs self-serve user administration with scoped access and two-administrator approval, which the fraud tools could reuse. (Account Incident Manager (AIM) · Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) · Discover Partner Product Portal · Discover Network Service Center · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Issuers: large banks, Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors
6b.11Give intermediaries a multi-institution queue and give the client a viewModerate evidence
The move
Let a processor or CUSO work cases for many clients in one queue, while each client sees its own cases read-only.
Why it wins
Small issuers and fintechs reach networks through processors and learn outcomes late or never. Amex OptBlue merchants see no network screen at all. Today a processor analyst needs a user ID per institution and queues are private to their creator, though a view-only role already exists. (Card Dispute Consultant · Disputes · Supervisor, Dispute Operations (Velera) · How to Manage · Chargeback Analyst at Stax · Discover Global Network Disputes)
For
Issuers: community banks and credit unions, Payment facilitators and ISOs, Fintechs and programme managers
6b.12Structured ATM claims built on the journalThin evidence
The move
Ask for named journal fields in ATM claims and responses in place of free-text memos.
Why it wins
Visa names the disbursement record fields while Mastercard codes ATM cases as free text, and operators already hold the journal. (Visa Core Rules · Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition · ATM Services)
For
ATM operators

How it works, by partner type

Issuers: large banks

NetworkHow it worksTools and screensFriction
VisaThe issuer must report fraud to Visa before it can raise a fraud dispute, within 60 days of the transaction (Visa Core Rules). An analyst logs into VROL, searches the transaction, records provisional credit, opens a dispute case and completes a dynamic questionnaire (Visa Risk-based Auto Dispute · Visa Core Rules). Fraud and authorisation disputes follow the Allocation flow, where Visa assigns liability and the acquirer can only pre-arbitrate within 30 days (Visa Dispute Management Service · Visa Core Rules). Consumer and processing disputes follow the Collaboration flow, where the issuer makes the pre-arbitration attempt within 30 days of the acquirer's response (Visa Core Rules). Arbitration must be filed within 10 days of the pre-arbitration response, and a missed deadline closes the cycle against the silent party (Visa Core Rules). Time limits vary by condition. Authorisation disputes allow 75 days against 120 for most fraud and consumer disputes (Visa Core Rules). Before a dispute exists, VROL checks Order Insight and Rapid Dispute Resolution. RDR-resolved cases close with status Merchant Credit (Compelling Evidence 3.0 · Rapid Dispute Resolution). Issuers with excessive card-absent disputes or fraud enter VIMP, with assessments rising to USD 100,000 a month (Visa Core Rules). Compromised-account alerts arrive only inside Visa Risk Manager, and loss recovery needs fraud reported within 120 days of the alert (Account Data Compromise Best).Visa Resolve Online (VROL). Mandated web tool on Visa Online for the whole dispute cycle. Questions and documents must be in English (Vice President, Dispute Processing · Visa Core Rules). VROL dispute questionnaire. Sections for transaction, dispute request, elaboration, certifications, notes and documents, and issuer contact, as mirrored by a processor portal (iQ Reporting and Analytics). VROL Dispute Tracking Scorecard. Case tracking view used with Visa's outsourced dispute service (Visa Dispute Management Service). Visa Risk Manager. Rules, case, account and reporting modules over the Advanced Authorization score, plus an Alert API into the issuer back office (Visa Advanced Authorisation · Visa Risk Manager · Visa Core Rules). Dispute Doc Analyzer (2026). Summaries of merchant documents for issuer analysts, pitched against slow manual review (Visa Unveils New Services).Compelling Evidence 3.0 reaches the issuer as a Visa rejection code with no dispute right left, and ICBA says it shifts liability and call-centre work to issuers (Managing Visa Disputes · How Visa's Updated Compelling). Arbitration is decided on prior exchanges only, and an appeal needs new evidence and at least USD 5,000 at stake (Visa Core Rules). Fraud-reporting failures can suspend fraud dispute rights for 90 or 180 days, turning an administrative lapse into direct losses (Visa Core Rules). Every US issuer pays Advanced Authorization fees whether or not it uses the data (Visa Core Rules).
MastercardThe issuer opens one claim in Mastercom, and every later event hangs off that claim ID (Mastercom · Mastercard Developers llms.txt index). A fraud chargeback needs a prior Fraud and Loss Database report, which the issuer can file from inside the claim (Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition · Mastercom Use Cases). Evidence must reach Mastercom within eight days, second presentment comes within 45, and pre-arbitration within 30 after that (Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition). If the acquirer rejects pre-arbitration, the issuer has 15 days to escalate to arbitration or it bears the loss (Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition). Mastercom stamps some chargebacks as rejected before the acquirer sees them, including 5002 for First-Party Trust (Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI · Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition). Ethoca Consumer Clarity data is being linked into the claim record for issuer agents during 2026 (Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI · Mastercom Announcements). Transaction Summary Search takes 30-day windows starting within the past 730 days. The claim is then opened from the chosen row (Mastercom User Guide). Closing the Claim Editor mid-way parks the claim in state Pending until someone returns to it (Mastercom User Guide).Mastercom work queues. IssuerRepresentmentUnworked, IssuerWorked, Rejects, PendingDocumentation, SenderCaseFiling, ReceiverCaseFiling and Closed, among 13 queues (Mastercom Testing). Mastercom case filing. Case types 1 to 4, a mandatory memo up to 13,000 characters, statuses New to Ruled, and six ruling values such as Favor Sender (Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI). First-Party Trust evidence flag. The issuer must acknowledge merchant evidence before proceeding with a chargeback (Mastercom API v6 OpenAPI). Fraud and Loss Database. Batch, screen or API submission. Records land as confirmed, rejected or suspended (Confirmed Fraud · Confirmed Fraud (FLD)). Mastercom Claims Manager and Dispute Resolution tabs. Two main tabs. Hosted gives limited data for low volumes, and Pro adds all data elements, advanced filters and ad hoc reports (Mastercom User Guide). Claim Editor Apply Action menu. Only the events valid for the claim state, such as Create chargeback, Create case and Create Fraud and Loss Database Report (Mastercom User Guide). Mastercom dashboards. Widgets built from saved filters, with optional timed refresh, to spot urgent work (Mastercom User Guide). Case filing status icons. Letter icons for accepted, withdrawn, declined, expired and filed in error, and no icon while a case waits for a response (Mastercom User Guide).Overriding a First-Party Trust reject needs a notarised cardholder affidavit plus a closed and blocked account (Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition). Fraud chargebacks are capped at 35 per card account by the Fraud Notification Service (Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition). A claim opened in Mastercom v6 cannot be recreated in Mastercom Extended, so issuers track where each claim lives during migration (Mastercom Extended Claims use · Mastercard Developers llms.txt). Mastercard, which sells dispute tools, says US issuers spend about USD 9 to 10 per dispute (What is the true). Chargeback documents purge after 65 days unless a later cycle exists, while case filings stay up to three years (Mastercom User Guide). Expedited Billing Dispute Forms are filled in, saved to a local drive and then dragged onto the transaction (Mastercom User Guide).
American ExpressAmex first tries to resolve the disputed charge from its own information, then sends an Inquiry or a Chargeback (Merchant Regulations). On the GNS network, issuers file a First Chargeback within 120 days, and acquirers have 45 days to second present (Business and Operational Policies). GNS issuers must report confirmed fraud by the next business day after verification (Business and Operational Policies). The Global Disputes Monitoring Program holds each issuer and acquirer to monthly regional thresholds, 0.20 per cent in the US (Business and Operational Policies).AEGNS Network Disputes Manager (NDM). The licensed dispute system for all GNS documentation, with a USD 100 monthly licence and a free browser version, NDM Disputes Online (Business and Operational Policies). GNS FraudNet. Urgent Investigation Requests, the Participant Communication Platform and monthly fraud reports, reached after Knowledge Base access (Business and Operational Policies · Knowledge Base).Arbitration costs USD 150 to file and USD 250 for review, and a USD 100 penalty may be assessed when submission rules are not followed (Business and Operational Policies). The NDM and FraudNet user guides are on the gated Knowledge Base, so no screens are public (Knowledge Base).
Discover familyDiscover's dispute framework charges a dispute resolved for the cardholder back to the merchant or acquirer (Discover 10-K 2024). Issuer-side dispute screens and filing windows are not public. The Disputes Portal redirects straight to a sign-in (Discover Global Network · Fraud and Risk Center). Confirmed fraud is submitted through a separate Confirmed Fraud Portal enrolled by form (Confirmed Fraud Portal Access · Fraud and Risk Center). Compromise cases run through Account Incident Manager, shared between issuers, acquirers and the network (Account Incident Manager (AIM)). Diners Club franchises enrol in the same Account Incident Manager through a dedicated form section and mailbox (Account Incident Manager (AIM)). Since April 2021 issuers work Discover disputes in the DN Disputes Portal, starting from a Document Retrieval, Chargeback or Compliance tab (Discover Global Network Disputes). Opening a transaction creates a Dispute ID at once, but nothing is disputed until the issuer completes and submits the tab (Discover Global Network Disputes). After a representment the issuer may file a Pre-Arbitration Inquiry, then an Arbitration Request. Each can be withdrawn (Discover Global Network Disputes). An issuer can group several transactions under one Issuer Case Number. Each keeps its own Dispute ID for the acquirer to answer (Discover Global Network Disputes). Issuers may raise a compliance case on an undisputed transaction or one already decided for the merchant (Discover Global Network Disputes). During the move, users reached both the old DNDS and the new portal from the Account Center (Discover Global Network Disputes). Chargeback follow-ups are Update, Cancel and Chargeback Reversal, and each submit must wait for a green success message (Discover Global Network Disputes). A processor guide gives Discover fraud chargebacks 30 days after a retrieval closes or 120 days from processing, whichever is later (Dispute Best Practices). Discover retrieval codes include 6041 for fraud analysis and 6040 for a good faith request (Dispute Best Practices).Discover Network Disputes Portal. Gated behind the same identity provider as the Partner Product Portal. Nothing readable without credentials (Discover Global Network · Discover Partner Product Portal). Fraud and Risk Center. Login hub for Account Incident Manager, Confirmed Fraud, Fraud Alerts and High Brand Risk, with email-only MFA since 2025 (Fraud and Risk Center · Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)). DN Disputes Portal Transaction Search. Tabs for Account Number, Dispute ID or Case Number, Merchant Number and NRID or RRN, with a three-month date limit and a 1,000-result cap (Discover Global Network Disputes). DN Disputes Portal Dispute Details page. Dispute ID, Case Number, Stage Expiration and Dispute Status above Dispute Action Tabs, with comments, notices and documents at the foot of each tab (Discover Global Network Disputes). My Queue and Disputes search queues. A personal queue of assigned items, plus saved filter queues that update as cases change stage and are visible only to their creator (Discover Global Network Disputes). Daily Issuer Disputes Report (DIDR) and Daily Issuer Processor Disputes Report (DIPR). Account Center reports with Dispute Detail, Reason Code Summary and Notice Type Summary sections for each IIN range (Discover Global Network Disputes). Dispute Activity. Inbound or outbound actions by party ID over at most seven days, with export and bulk notice download of up to 50 PDFs (Discover Global Network Disputes).Fraud tool enrolment needs two named administrators, a Director or VP signature and an emailed form (Account Incident Manager (AIM)). The portal shows some reason codes differently from the Dispute Rules Manual and technical specifications, so staff translate between documents (Discover Global Network Disputes). Dispute Status values such as Update Completed and Unable to Process describe the system result and say nothing about who acts next (Discover Global Network Disputes). Passwords expire every 30 days, and accounts unused for 90 days are deleted and must be rebuilt by an administrator (Discover Global Network Disputes). Every administrator change needs a second administrator to approve it, so two named administrators are the minimum (Discover Global Network Disputes). Reports sit in the separate Account Center under Operations Reports, away from the cases they describe (Discover Global Network Disputes). Users must set up spare sign-in methods at first login, because the guide says they cannot be added later (Discover Global Network Disputes). Comments allow 1 to 750 characters from a short list of special characters, and any other character raises an error (Discover Global Network Disputes).

Best pattern. Mastercard's claim model is the best issuer pattern: one claim ID from intake to ruling, fraud reporting inside the claim, and named queues with hard deadline edits (Mastercom · Mastercom Use Cases · Mastercom Testing · Mastercom Code and Formats). Discover today. Discover's issuer dispute experience is not publicly visible. Fraud reporting and compromise cases sit in separate portals enrolled by signed forms (Discover Global Network · Confirmed Fraud Portal Access · Account Incident Manager (AIM)).

What public sources could not show

  1. VROL screens, queue names and API case states The VROL API reference is a restricted product and no republished user guide or training video was found. Visa University dispute course outlines, a sponsor issuer or processor walk-through, or processor user guides that mirror VROL.
  2. Mastercom user interface screens The current Mastercom guide sits on the Technical Resource Center behind Mastercard Connect. A 2022 edition posted by a processor shows the screens, but later changes are not public. A processor or CUSO demo, or Mastercard Developers reference apps on GitHub.
  3. Discover Network Disputes Portal and PULSE Disputes System Both are behind login, and the Dispute Rules Manual and PULSE rules are not public. Archived manuals marked confidential were not used. Ask Discover's own partner teams through proper channels, or observe a partner acquirer walk-through.
  4. Amex NDM and FraudNet screens User guides sit on the gated GNS Knowledge Base. A GNS partner walk-through or any future public training webinar.
  5. VAMP and ECP notifications and reports The VAMP Guide and Mastercard's Data Integrity manual are non-public, and ECP thresholds appear only through practitioners. Acquirer merchant notices republished publicly, or acquirer compliance staff interviews.
  6. Network dispute fee schedules Visa and Mastercard fee amounts are not published. Figures come from vendors and processors. Processor pricing pass-through notices and published merchant fee schedules.
  7. Visa's 2026 dispute products beyond the announcement Dispute Intelligence, Dispute Recovery Manager and the Dispute Resolution Network have no public product pages. Later Visa product pages, demos or conference sessions.
  8. Interac and Diners partner dispute handling The search budget ran out before Interac was checked, and no public Diners issuer or acquirer dispute guide was found. Interac member rules summaries and Diners franchise materials, if public.
  9. Mastercard Collaboration shutdown bulletin The primary bulletin is gated, so the January 2027 end date rests on one consultancy. Acquirer notices to merchants or a second practitioner source.

Run: change, support and incidents

Every network pushes change through gated bulletins on a fixed calendar. Visa emails weekly Visa Business News to two named roles, Mastercard posts numbered announcements on its login-only Technical Resource Center (Visa Core Rules · Chargebacks Made Simple Guide · AN 6977 Revised Standards). American Express publishes a monthly Network Participant Updates bulletin and April and October manuals. Discover updates its programme documents twice a year, and processors report dated April Discover and PULSE releases (American Express Global Network · Business and Operational Policies · Discover 10-K 2024 · Card Network Certifications 2026). The primary bulletins are private. Visa says its Business News articles are not public, Mastercard bulletins reach only members through Mastercard Connect, and PULSE publishes no rules or bulletins on its public site (Visa Merchant Business News · Mastercard GMAP Explained · Client Support). Most partners meet change second hand. Issuer processors republish each mandate with an impact note, and merchant processors count continued use as acceptance. One credit union CUSO asks clients to forward network mail (Card Network Mandates · Card Network Certifications 2026 · June 2026 Card Brand · Cards & Payments). American Express types each change as policy, legal or information only and publishes a route to a three-month extension. Visa waivers go through a representative and Mastercard variances through Variance Manager (Business and Operational Policies · Visa Core Rules · Mastercard Rules). Support runs through phone desks, mailboxes and named account executives. Mastercard and Visa describe 24x7 client support teams, Discover splits a 24x7 command centre from a business-hours operations centre, and PULSE publishes Central-time business hours only (Customer Technical Services Analyst · Client Services and Support · Contact Us · Connect With Us). No public status page for core authorisation and settlement was found for any of the four networks. Public status pages cover developer APIs and gateway products, and Amex posts urgent bulletins inside its Knowledge Base (API Status · Visa Acceptance Solutions Status · Mastercard Status · Insights). The clearest public account of incident communication failure is Visa's June 2018 outage. An independent review found its communications were not timely, regular or actionable, and the UK regulator now requires annual testing with participants (Specific Direction 9). Acquirers feel the strain most. The UK regulator found acquirers holding over 65 percent of the market struggle to get timely answers, and a US payfac filing calls network compliance timelines highly compressed (MR22/1.10 Market review · Priority Technology Holdings 10-K). Discover and PULSE change lightly. Two issuer processors say recent Discover and PULSE mandates did not affect them or their clients, which is an asset the network does not yet present (Card Network Mandates · Card Network Certifications 2026).

Design moves at this stage

6c.1Change ledger with a verdict per partnerStrong evidence
The move
Publish every rule, fee and specification change as one ledger item typed action, legal or information, with audience, region and effective date. Show each partner a verdict: acts, processor has handled it, or nothing needed.
Why it wins
Amex types changes and Mastercard headers carry action indicators, but no network tells a partner whether its processor has already absorbed the work. Processors write that sentence today. (Business and Operational Policies · AN 6977 Revised Standards · April 2026 Release Guide · Card Network Mandates · Card Network Certifications 2026)
For
all
6c.2Notices built to be forwardedStrong evidence
The move
Render each change as a shareable page with a public summary and role-specific views for processor, institution and merchant. Let a processor or CUSO subscribe clients and see who opened it.
Why it wins
Visa and Mastercard bulletins are private, and a CUSO relies on clients forwarding network mail. A forwardable notice makes the relay chain part of the network's own product. (Visa Merchant Business News · Mastercard GMAP Explained · Cards & Payments · Visa Rules Update Affecting · June 2026 Card Brand)
For
community banks, credit unions, ATM operators, payment facilitators and ISOs, merchants
6c.3Stated lead times on every changeStrong evidence
The move
Commit to a minimum notice period for fee and mandate changes worldwide, show it on each item, and flag any item that falls short with the reason.
Why it wins
Acquirers and payfacs describe compressed timelines. The UK now requires six months and Canada 120 days, so a global commitment turns regulation into a promise. (PS26/1 Market review · Code of Conduct · MR22/1.10 Market review · Priority Technology Holdings 10-K · Notification of Specification Changes)
For
acquirers and processors, payment facilitators and ISOs, issuers
6c.4Partner status for the core networkStrong evidence
The move
Run a partner status view for authorisation, settlement, portals and APIs, with subscriptions, a declared update rhythm during incidents and a post-incident report every partner can read.
Why it wins
Networks publish status only for APIs and gateway products. Visa's 2018 communications failed, while Mastercard shares post-incident reports only through account managers. (API Status · Mastercard Status · Insights · Visa Acceptance Solutions Status · Specific Direction 9 · Director, Technology Account Management · When Your Partners Fail · Capital One outage spans)
For
all
6c.5Extension request inside the changeModerate evidence
The move
Attach a request-more-time action to each change, with the decision rule stated up front and a tracked status.
Why it wins
Amex publishes a three-month extension route that will not be unreasonably withheld. Visa routes waivers through a representative with a fee, and large PSPs staff people to chase waivers. (Business and Operational Policies · Visa Core Rules · Mastercard Rules · Program Manager, Card Network)
For
issuers, acquirers and processors, payment facilitators and ISOs
6c.6One support map with hours and clocksModerate evidence
The move
Publish one support map by partner type and problem, each route with hours and a response commitment, and a round-the-clock path for small institutions.
Why it wins
Discover and PULSE spread support across many mailboxes and business-hours desks. Acquirers struggle to get timely answers, and SHAZAM shows small institutions value 24/7 service. (Contact Us · Connect With Us · Contact Us · MR22/1.10 Market review · Ethoca Alerts for Merchants)
For
all
6c.7Contacts that stay currentModerate evidence
The move
Let partners assign roles for change, incident and compliance notices, send each notice to several people, and prompt a review when a contact bounces or goes quiet.
Why it wins
Visa's rules treat a notice as received when sent and rely on two named roles. Mastercard leaves credential expiry tracking to customers. (Visa Core Rules · Business and Operational Policies · Support)
For
issuers, acquirers and processors
6c.8A quiet cycle, said plainlyModerate evidence
The move
When a release asks nothing of a partner, say so from the network, by name and date.
Why it wins
Processors report that recent Discover and PULSE releases needed nothing from clients. A light change burden is a real benefit that only processors voice today. (Card Network Certifications 2026 · Card Network Mandates)
For
fintechs and programme managers, community banks, credit unions
6c.9Operational review for every partnerThin evidence
The move
Assemble a periodic review from each partner's own record: changes applied, incidents, open cases and attestations due. Offer it to partners without an account manager.
Why it wins
Mastercard runs quarterly operational reviews for key accounts and Visa writes client success plans. Small card teams rarely get either. That last point is inference. (Director, Technology Account Management · Director Client Success · Contact Us · Card Services Manager)
For
issuers, acquirers and processors, community banks, credit unions

How it works, by partner type

Large issuers (national and regional banks)

NetworkHow it worksTools and screensFriction
VisaVisa sends weekly Visa Business News by email to each member's Primary Center Manager and Senior Officer. The Primary Center Manager must distribute it inside the bank (Visa Core Rules). Members register these roles in the My Organization's Contacts module of the Client Directory in Visa Access. Updates are due within 10 business days of a change (Visa Core Rules). A Business News article carries an article ID, a region and audience line, a brand line and an overview with the effective date (Article ID AI09108). Visa corrects an article by republishing it with a note on what changed (Article ID AI09108). A Visa Notification takes effect when Visa sends it, so a missed email is still a received notice (Visa Core Rules). Regional implementation analysts project-manage the twice-yearly business enhancement releases and Visa mandates for clients and processors (Implementation Analyst). A bank that cannot comply asks for a waiver through its Visa representative. Visa answers in writing, each waiver is unique, and an extension carries an assessment (Visa Core Rules). For log-in and technical issues users go to their own delegated administrators first, then a regional Visa Access Support team by email or phone (Visa Access Support). Issuers and acquirers without Visa Access are told to contact their Visa account executive or manager (Visa Access Support). A Client Success manager owns post-sale service and a Client Success Plan, separate from the account team (Director Client Success). During issuer outages Visa's Smarter Stand-In Processing authorises on the issuer's behalf (Visa 10-K 2025).Visa Access (formerly Visa Online). Password-protected client site for members and processors, claiming 150+ services, with a built-in help centre and AI search (Visa Core Rules · Log · Visa Access). Client Directory: My Organization's Contacts. Where a member names its Primary Center Manager and Senior Officer, who then receive Visa Business News (Visa Core Rules). Visa Business News. Weekly email bulletin with article ID, region, audience, brand and effective-dated overview (Visa Core Rules · Article ID AI09108). Visa Resolve Online. Mandated web application for dispute life-cycle work by issuer and acquirer staff (Vice President, Dispute Processing).There is no public archive of Visa Business News, so anyone outside the two named roles depends on internal forwarding (Visa Core Rules · Visa Merchant Business News). During the June 2018 outage Visa's methods for reaching clients were found not effective or efficient (Specific Direction 9). Waiver extensions cost money and set no precedent, so each bank relitigates similar requests (Visa Core Rules).
MastercardMastercard defines its Standards to include announcements and bulletins, which is how rule changes take effect (Mastercard Rules). Announcements are posted in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect. Each has a structured header with type, audience, region, action indicator, published and effective dates (Chargebacks Made Simple Guide · AN 6977 Revised Standards). Each rulebook edition opens with a summary of changes mapped to numbered announcements with regional prefixes (Mastercard Rules). Network releases are named by year and quarter, with major releases in April and October (Card Network Certifications 2026). Urgent issues go by phone to Customer Technical Services. Non-urgent ones go to a Support Case Management tool (Mastercard Rules · Release Notes and Dates). Customer Technical Services is described as a single point of contact giving first and second level support around the clock (Customer Technical Services Analyst). Technology account managers run Quarterly Operational Reviews for key accounts and train customers on releases (Director, Technology Account Management). In an incident the account manager joins the response team, relays updates, and later shares Mastercard's Post Incident Report (Director, Technology Account Management). A bank that cannot meet a Standard requests a variance through Variance Manager on Mastercard Connect (Mastercard Rules). Noncompliance assessments can be appealed to the Chief Franchise Officer within 30 days, for a fee of up to USD 500 (Mastercard Rules).Mastercard Connect. Sign-in wall with RSA SecurID for Mastercom, Technical Resource Center, My Company Manager and Variance Manager (Mastercard Connect (sign-in)). Technical Resource Center. Announcements and bulletins, plus guides such as the Chargeback Guide and Mastercom User Guide (Announcements · Support). Support Case Management. Case application on Mastercard Connect for non-urgent support (Release Notes and Dates). Variance Manager. Tool for requesting a variance from a Standard (Mastercard Rules).The Technical Resource Center returns a 404 to unauthenticated visitors, so change news reaches the public only through practitioners (Announcements · Mastercard GMAP Explained). Mastercard's Atlassian status page appears to be an unpopulated template (Mastercard Status). Quarterly reviews appear in postings for key accounts only, so smaller issuers may never see one. That is inference (Director, Technology Account Management).
American ExpressNetwork Participant Updates publish monthly on the second Friday, and Special Bulletins cover urgent issues (American Express Global Network). The Business and Operational Policies manual is republished every April and October and posted to Knowledge Base (Business and Operational Policies). Each change is typed Policy, Legally required or Information only (Business and Operational Policies). Policy changes take effect on publication. A participant that cannot comply documents the impact and requests up to three months' extension, which Amex says it will not unreasonably withhold (Business and Operational Policies). Technical specification changes are announced six months ahead in a twice-yearly Notification of Specification Changes (Notification of Specification Changes). Participants sign an annual attestation of accuracy for Program Progress Reports (Business and Operational Policies). An issuer schedules its own outages by phoning the AEGNS Help Desk, ideally 30 days ahead, and must report unscheduled outages at once (Business and Operational Policies). Violations follow a determination, notification and Action Plan process with escalating fees (Business and Operational Policies). Training is requested through the Amex representative or a named mailbox and assigned by Knowledge Base profile (Partners · Partner Learning). What public sources could not show

  1. The Visa Business News library and notification settings inside Visa Access. Visa says the articles are not public and the portal needs a Business ID. Look for Visa Access help-centre videos, Visa University course outlines and articles that banks or processors republish, such as the AI09108 PDF.
  2. Mastercard's Technical Resource Center announcement list, filters and email subscriptions. The site returns 404 without login, and a public training video sits behind a bot check. Search for customer training decks and processor onboarding guides that include TRC screenshots.
  3. How Discover and PULSE write and send their bulletins, and the lead times they give. No Discover or PULSE bulletin is public, and processors only confirm the releases exist. Check court exhibits, state procurement records and credit union processor notices that quote Discover or PULSE release text.
  4. The EASI Message Center and Document Library, and the Release Compliance Tool. All three need registration or an NDA. Look for processor certification guides and job postings that describe EASI or RCT work.
  5. What networks send issuers and acquirers during their own outages. Only the 2018 Visa case is documented, and manuals describe partners reporting to the network. Read Bank of England and PSR post-incident material, and trade press on later outages.
  6. Business review agendas, scorecards and client success plans. They are contractual and appear only in job postings. Search public-sector card programme contracts and RFP responses that attach account management plans.
  7. Waiver, variance and extension request forms and their decision times. Forms sit in Visa Access, Mastercard Connect and Knowledge Base. Look for court exhibits and regulator filings that quote waiver correspondence, such as the DOJ's Visa case.
  8. Discover and Amex account-team job descriptions from 2026. The live Capital One posting had expired and this session's web search budget ran out. Rerun a job-board sweep for Discover Global Network and Amex GNS account roles.

Growing the relationship, and leaving it

After go-live, every network routes growth through a named relationship owner: Visa's Client Success manager and account team, Mastercard's account managers, Amex relationship managers and Discover account executives (Director Client Success · Visa Ready Program · Associate Analyst, Account Management · American Express Certification · Contact Us). Self-service ordering exists only in patches. Mastercard Connect has a Store with Request, checkout and Track Orders, and Amex has Service Enrollment inside Knowledge Base (Mastercard Connect Overview 2022 · Partners · Partner Learning Solutions). Visa sends community issuers to a product enrolment portal on Visa Online. Discover enrols fraud products by PDF application or web form, and PULSE enrols new clients through an account executive (Visa Community Issuer Resources · Community Solutions · Fraud and Risk Center · Fraud Detection & Risk). Incentives are the main commercial lever, worth 15.75 billion dollars at Visa and 20.5 billion at Mastercard in their 2025 years (Visa 10-K 2025 · Mastercard 10-K 2025). Both networks estimate what a partner has earned from volume, card issuance and card conversion forecasts, and Visa uses client-reported data as one input (Visa 10-K 2025 · Mastercard 10-K 2025). Tracking happens inside the network. Job postings describe incentive tracking files, Power BI dashboards, an Oracle billing system and regional quarterly incentive reviews (Client Incentive Performance Finance · Financial Analyst · Manager, Deal Management). The study found no public sign of a partner-facing incentive tracker at any network. This is a gap in the public record, and it may exist behind login (Manager, Deal Management · Financial Analyst). Mastercard contracts carry clawbacks and customer commitments, and DOJ alleges Visa can claw back paid incentives as early termination fees (Manager, Deal Management · United States v. Visa). Exit is written into the Mastercard and Visa rulebooks, and it is heavy. Maestro and Cirrus principals give a year's notice, cards must be cancelled and fees are not refunded (Mastercard Rules). A Visa member cannot finish leaving until every BIN is released, and a BIN must sit inactive for 120 days first (Visa Core Rules). Conversions are paid for and tooled towards the incumbent. Visa Account Updater carries Mastercard, Amex and Discover portfolios into Visa, and outside Latin America it carries none out (Visa Account Updater (VAU) · Visa Consulting and Analytics). Consulting is a paid line at Visa and Mastercard, and UK acquirers say they buy scheme services just to understand their own fees (Visa 10-K 2025 · Mastercard 10-K 2025 · MR22/1.10 Market review · MR22/1.6 consultation responses). The Discover family's strongest growth asset is the PULSE Debit Dashboard, open to every PULSE issuer, with interchange by category and a peer comparison (Unlock the Value). Discover's owner ran the largest recent conversion, about 25 million debit cards, and merchants and processors bore visible costs from it (Capital One 10-K 2025 · After Moving Debit Cards · Changes following Capital One's). Regulators are opening renewal and exit. Canada lets merchants cancel penalty-free within 70 days of a fee rise, and the UK and Australia now require fee transparency (Code of Conduct · PS26/1: Market review · Transparency of Wholesale Fees). The public record is thin on business review content, incentive statements and exit terms at Amex and Discover. Those sit in gated manuals and contracts (American Express Global Network · Discover 10-K 2024 · Partner Learning).

Design moves at this stage

7.1One catalogue with Request and order trackingStrong evidence
The move
List every service with an Included or Priced marker, a Request action scoped to BINs, approver sign-off, and a tracked order.
Why it wins
Mastercard's Connect Store sets the pattern, while Discover enrols by PDF, form or account executive. (Mastercard Connect Overview 2022 · Fraud and Risk Center · Fraud Detection & Risk · Discover Developer Center FAQ)
For
Large issuers, Community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors, ATM operators, Developers
7.2Business review built on shared dataStrong evidence
The move
Extend the Debit Dashboard model across the family and generate the review from what the partner already sees.
Why it wins
PULSE already gives every issuer economics with peers, and its account executive says most issuers do not know their interchange. (Unlock the Value · Visa Analytics Platform · Portfolio Advisor for Approval)
For
Community banks and credit unions, Large issuers, Acquirers and processors
7.3Incentive ledger in the partner recordModerate evidence
The move
Show each commitment, its measure, the partner's standing, who supplied the data, and payment status, including any clawback trigger.
Why it wins
Visa and Mastercard track incentives in internal files, billing systems and quarterly reviews, and no partner-facing tracker was found. (Client Incentive Performance Finance · Financial Analyst · Manager, Deal Management · Visa 10-K 2025)
For
Large issuers, Community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors, Merchants
7.4Conversion desk for issuers moving inModerate evidence
The move
Plan reissue waves, updater coverage, merchant notices, PIN changes and country acceptance gaps as a tracked conversion plan.
Why it wins
Visa tools and consults for inbound conversion, and credit unions leave members to fix stored cards and PINs. (Visa Account Updater (VAU) · Visa Consulting and Analytics · Debit Card Update · Mastercard Debit Upgrade · Changes following Capital One's · Capital One Tests Moving)
For
Community banks and credit unions, Large issuers, Fintechs and programme managers
7.5Written exit terms with a leaving checklistModerate evidence
The move
Publish what leaving requires and what survives, including BIN release, cardholder and merchant notices, data export and transfer help.
Why it wins
Mastercard and Visa publish exit rules. Discover publishes none, and its owner competes with partner issuers. (Mastercard Rules · Visa Core Rules · Discover 10-K 2024 · Capital One 10-K 2025)
For
Large issuers, Community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors, Fintechs and programme managers, ATM operators
7.6Renewal workspace over the whole termModerate evidence
The move
Open renewal early with term economics, services used, commitments met and an incumbent-incentive line the partner fills in.
Why it wins
Networks renew in advance, consultants win by negotiating, and regulators are forcing fee clarity. (American Express 10-K 2025 · Payments Card Networks Advisors · Scheme Fees · Code of Conduct)
For
Large issuers, Community banks and credit unions, Acquirers and processors
7.7Growth paths inside the recordModerate evidence
The move
Show the next step, such as a new country, role or threshold, with eligibility and what changes.
Why it wins
Mastercard and Amex publish growth steps and thresholds, and Discover's growth happens case by case. (Mastercard Rules · OptBlue Program Update · Visa Core Rules · Moorwand Ltd Expands Its)
For
Acquirers and processors, Payment facilitators and ISOs, Fintechs and programme managers
7.8Fee explanation included, consulting on requestModerate evidence
The move
Explain each fee line inside the product at no charge, and offer diagnostic consulting as a visible request.
Why it wins
UK acquirers pay schemes to understand their own bills, while Visa and Mastercard sell consulting as a line. (MR22/1.10 Market review · MR22/1.6 consultation responses · Mastercard 10-K 2025 · Visa Consulting and Analytics)
For
Acquirers and processors, Large issuers, Community banks and credit unions

How it works, by partner type

Large issuers (large banks and co-brand issuers)

NetworkHow it worksTools and screensFriction
VisaVisa signs long-term incentive contracts with banks and estimates each client's earnings from volume, card issuance and card conversion forecasts (Visa 10-K 2025). A Client Incentive Operations team loads each contract into Oracle Revenue Management and Billing, schedules payments and checks with clients whether obligations were met (Financial Analyst). A Client Success manager owns a Client Success Plan and post-sale service, beside a separate account team (Director Client Success). Growth offers include Visa Consulting and Analytics, run as Diagnose, Align, Roadmap and Implement, and the self-service Visa Analytics Platform with peer benchmarks (Visa Consulting and Analytics · Visa 10-K 2025 · Visa Analytics Platform). Visa says some clients can leave on relatively short notice without significant fees. DOJ alleges a debit issuer missing growth targets could owe earned benefits back plus a fixed fee (Visa 10-K 2025 · United States v. Visa). To leave, a member releases every BIN after 120 inactive days and stays liable for earlier exceptions and fees (Visa Core Rules). BINs cannot be sold, so a portfolio sale is notified to Visa, and a buyer that is not a member files within 10 days or stops (Visa Core Rules).Visa Access Client Portfolio Management Self-Service Tools. Program Request Management, the electronic Client Information Questionnaire and the Visa Client Support Application, for Visa profile and programme changes (Visa Core Rules · Log). Client Directory in Visa Access. Member contacts and service providers, which members must update within 10 business days of a change (Visa Core Rules). Visa Analytics Platform. Self-service dashboards on portfolio, fraud, approvals and disputes against a competitive peer set (Visa Analytics Platform · Visa 10-K 2025). Oracle Revenue Management and Billing (internal). Visa's own system for incentive contract set-up and payments. Partners do not see it (Financial Analyst).DOJ alleges nearly 1,000 Visa issuing contracts carry volume incentives that deter adding debit networks (United States v. Visa). DOJ alleges issuers rarely change network, partly because reissuing cards is costly (United States v. Visa). An analyst expects Visa would reverse discounts across a defecting bank's whole portfolio. This is opinion with no disclosed term behind it (Fiserv debit network sale).
MastercardMastercard pays rebates and incentives when customers meet volume thresholds, and estimates performance from card issuance and card conversion volumes (Mastercard 10-K 2025). Deal managers monitor contracts, calculate incentive payments, join regional quarterly incentive reviews and discuss deal performance with customers (Manager, Deal Management). Drafted contracts are checked against the approved business case, including term, clawbacks and customer commitments (Manager, Deal Management). Mastercard says its data services help it win new and renewed deals, and account teams build revenue and expense benchmarks for customers (Mastercard 10-K 2025 · Associate Analyst, Account Management). In January 2026 Mastercard renewed Capital One's credit partnership and kept a large portion of newly acquired credit accounts (Mastercard reworks Cap One). Mastercard says customers can reassess commitments within their contract terms, and its Advisors consulting line sells strategy and implementation help (Mastercard 10-K 2025 · Advisors and transformation). Mastercard may also end a licence after 26 weeks without activity or when a customer falls short of its approved business plan (Mastercard Rules). To leave, a Principal gives 30 days' notice for a Mastercard licence and a year for Maestro or Cirrus, then cancels cards and notifies cardholders (Mastercard Rules). A portfolio sale needs 30 days' written notice to Mastercard, and a terminated customer gets no refund of fees (Mastercard Rules).Mastercard Connect Store. Applications and reports a company can request, each with a Request button, a checkout form scoping data by ICA, BIN or account range, and Track Orders (Mastercard Connect Overview 2022). Pricing and Billing Resource Center. The Pricing Guide and a Transaction Detail tool, requested through the Connect Store (Mastercard Connect Overview 2022). Mastercard Business Intelligence (Portfolio Advisor). Self-service approval recommendations from competitive benchmarks and past performance (Portfolio Advisor for Approval). Variance Manager. Requests to depart from a Mastercard standard, with a stated reason (Mastercard Rules).Mastercard warns it may have to raise incentives and discounts to meet customer demand for better pricing (Mastercard 10-K 2025). From April 2026 Mastercard added services to a US bundle fee and raised its rate, per a merchant advisory (April 2026 Release Guide).
American ExpressEach GNS issuer's rate is negotiated individually and not published (American Express 10-K 2025). Amex offers licensed issuers data and analytics with benchmarking and best practice, plus predictive models for marketing (Partners). New value-added capabilities are certified through the issuer's relationship manager, who supplies scripts and test cases (American Express Certification). Cobrand deals run for a fixed period, and Amex seeks renewal before the term ends (American Express 10-K 2025). Some cobrand partners may buy the card loans, or name a buyer, when the deal ends. Amex may not renew its Amazon and Lowe's small business portfolios (American Express 10-K 2025). Amex cites its 2016 loss of Costco in the US as an example of non-renewal (American Express 10-K 2025). The Amazon business cards moved to U.S. Bank on Mastercard, with Amex cardholders migrating on 14 August 2026 (Amazon's New Prime Business). Amex itself exited GNS licensing in the EU and Australia and terminated existing EU licences after regulation (American Express 10-K 2017 · American Express 10-K 2025).Knowledge Base Service Enrollment. One place to read about each network service and enrol directly (Partners · Partner Learning Solutions). Partner Analytics Center. A partner reporting tool known only from a September 2021 training replay title (Partner Learning · Partner Learning Solutions). Network Partner Learning. Training assigned by Knowledge Base profile, including a card acquisition campaign webinar (Partner Learning Solutions).The public webinar list stops at June 2022, so current growth training is not visible (Partner Learning Solutions). Exit terms sit in the gated Business and Operational Policies manual (American Express Global Network).
Discover familyDiscover enters fixed-term pricing or incentive deals with some participants and competes on incentives and rebates, publishing no amounts (Discover 10-K 2024). Its deferred incentive balance was 28 million dollars at end-2024, against billions at Visa and Mastercard (Discover 10-K 2024 · Visa 10-K 2025 · Mastercard 10-K 2025). The owner says rival networks give issuers large signing bonuses and hold long, sometimes exclusive, bank deals (Capital One 10-K 2025). Capital One moved about 25 million debit cards onto the network and is testing new and converted credit accounts (Capital One 10-K 2025 · After Moving Debit Cards · Capital One Tests Moving). Venture X and several co-brands stay on Visa, and Capital One names Mexico, the Caribbean, Canada and the UK as acceptance priorities (After Moving Debit Cards · Capital One Tests Moving). Diners Club International sells an exclusive issuer franchise per market, applied for by email (Diners Club International Issuing).Discover Global Network Account Executive. Named owner of contracts, technical upgrades and configuration changes (Contact Us). Service Center enrolment. Application PDFs and web forms for Account Incident Manager, Confirmed Fraud, Fraud Alerts and High Brand Risk (Fraud and Risk Center).Capital One warns it may be unable to offer network partners adequate pricing while keeping enough net revenue (Capital One 10-K 2025). The network's owner competes with partner issuers and bought Brex, a corporate card rival to fintech partners (Capital One 10-K 2025 · Capital One to Acquire).

Best pattern. Mastercard publishes exit in its public rulebook: a notice table by licence type, portfolio sale notice, card cancellation and a duty to help merchants move (Mastercard Rules). Discover today. Discover publishes no issuer incentive terms or exit steps, and its owner's own conversion is the reference case. Relationships run through account executives (Discover 10-K 2024 · Contact Us · Capital One 10-K 2025).

What public sources could not show

  1. Partner-facing incentive statements or trackers inside Visa Access, the Mastercard Pricing and Billing Resource Center, the Amex Partner Analytics Center or the PULSE portal. All four are behind login, and job postings describe only internal tracking. Watch Amex's 2021 Partner Analytics Center replay captions, and look for exhibits in United States v. Visa.
  2. Business review decks and scorecards networks show partners. No public copies were found. Search court exhibits, credit union board minutes and conference talks by network account staff.
  3. Visa voluntary termination notice periods and Amex GNS exit terms. Visa's public rules cover BIN release but not notice, and the Amex manual is gated. Read Visa U.S.A. certificate and bylaws filings, and any Amex terms republished by a licensee.
  4. Discover and PULSE rules on termination, portfolio transfer and incentive clawback. Operating regulations are not published. Check processor release notes and issuer notices from banks leaving or joining PULSE.
  5. Whether Discover's account updater supports conversions into or out of Discover. No public statement was found. Read the Discover Network Account Updater page on the Partner Product Portal and processor guides.
  6. The current Mastercard Connect Store screens. The public overview dates from 2022. Search newer Connect guides that banks and processors republish.
  7. How Visa Consulting and Analytics and Mastercard Advisors are priced or bundled into deals. Neither publishes pricing. Search public-sector card programme tenders, which sometimes disclose network services.
  8. Growth and exit steps for ATM operators and payfacs at Discover and Visa. No public procedures were found. Ask ATM industry associations and read sponsor bank programme guides.

What no public source shows

  1. Signed-in screens of the incumbents' partner tools, such as Visa Access, VROL and VSS, Mastercard Connect and Mastercom, and the Amex Knowledge Base. Ask an acquirer or processor partner for a screen walk, and mine bank and processor guides, Visa University and Mastercard Academy course outlines and webinar captions.
  2. The invoices, settlement reports and billing analytics screens partners actually receive from each network. Ask an ISO partner or NAC member for a redacted statement, and watch for the UK schemes' fee logic letters and Standard A fee guides due by July 2027.
  3. Partner-facing incentive statements, business review decks and scorecards at any network. Watch Amex's 2021 Partner Analytics Center replay captions, and search court exhibits in United States v. Visa and credit union board minutes.
  4. How large banks run network selections and what network sales teams present. Interview advisers such as Cornerstone or Engage fi and bank card executives, and read DOJ trial exhibits as they are filed.
  5. Discover's own gated surfaces: the signed-in Developer Center, EASI Message Center and Document Library, the Disputes Portal, the host simulator and PULSE rules. Discover's own teams can review them internally and compare them against this benchmark.
